java-fundamentals-sr4-02.reason: ambiguous: 'A subclass declaration' does not say the subclass method is static, and the JLS calls an instance method with that signature overriding (a compile-time error). The rewrite names both methods as static. (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr4-02.statement: A subclass static method with the same signature as a superclass static method overrides it.
java-fundamentals-sr4-02.explanation: The subclass method hides the superclass one: a call through a superclass-typed reference still runs the superclass's static method, because the compile-time type picks a class method.
java-fundamentals-sr4-02.misconception: Static methods participate in overriding like instance methods.

java-fundamentals-sr5-02.reason: ambiguous: 'an inherited public instance method with a body' also covers a default inherited from a second interface, which causes a compile-time error rather than winning. The rewrite names the superclass as the origin. Confirmed by JLS 8.4.8: a default is not inherited when 'No concrete method inherited by C from its direct superclass type has a signature that is a subsignature'. (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr5-02.statement: A public concrete instance method inherited from a class's superclass wins over a matching interface default.
java-fundamentals-sr5-02.explanation: A class does not inherit an interface default when a concrete method inherited from its superclass already has a matching signature, so the superclass method is the one that runs.

java-fundamentals-sr7-10.reason: source_problem: no Java SE 25 page supports the return-type case. JLS 6.5.5.1 forbids a type parameter in a static context, and JLS 8.1.3 defines static context only for statements, declarations and expressions, not method headers; JLS 8.1.2 only points back to 6.5.5.1. The rewrite tests the case 6.5.5.1 states ('must not appear in the body of a static method declared by C'), keeping the answer false. (final: fixed)
java-fundamentals-sr7-10.statement: Inside a static method of `class Box<T>`, a local variable can be declared with the class's type parameter `T`.
java-fundamentals-sr7-10.explanation: A class's type parameter may not be named in a static context such as a static method body, where no current instance exists, so a local variable of type T there is a compile-time error.
java-fundamentals-sr7-10.misconception: Static methods of a generic class have access to the class's type parameter.

java-fundamentals-sr1-09.reason: tell: permission verbs ('accepts', 'fits', 'can compile', 'inherits', 'overrides') appear only in false statements, 0T/9F. Rewording as 'returns true' keeps the fact and answer (false). (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr1-09.explanation: Integer.equals requires its argument to be an Integer holding the same int value. A Long argument yields false.
java-fundamentals-sr1-09.misconception: Numeric wrappers compare equal across wrapper types.

java-fundamentals-sr4-06.reason: tell: removes 'can compile' (permission-verb tell for false) and uses 'compiles', which leaned true 7T/2F. Same fact and answer (false). (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr4-06.statement: `class A{void f(Object x){}} class B extends A{@Override void f(String x){}}` compiles.
java-fundamentals-sr4-06.explanation: The subclass's f(String) overloads f(Object), so @Override makes this declaration a compile-time error.
java-fundamentals-sr4-06.misconception: @Override accepts an overload with a different parameter type.

java-fundamentals-sr5-04.reason: tell: removes 'accepts' (false-only permission verb) and balances 'compiles' toward false. Same fact and answer (false); JLS 9.4.1.2 confirmed. (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr5-04.statement: An interface declaring `default String toString() { return "x"; }` compiles.
java-fundamentals-sr5-04.explanation: An interface's default toString implementation produces a compile-time error because it matches a non-private Object method.
java-fundamentals-sr5-04.misconception: An interface default can provide an implementation of Object.toString.

java-fundamentals-sr5-06.reason: tell: removes 'accepts' (false-only permission verb); the hedge 'may' was balanced 2T/2F. Same fact and answer (false); JLS 8.9.2 confirmed. (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr5-06.statement: An enum class may declare its constructor with the `protected` access modifier.
java-fundamentals-sr5-06.explanation: Java rejects protected enum constructors at compile time. Enum constructors use private access, explicitly or implicitly.
java-fundamentals-sr5-06.misconception: Enum constructors support protected access like ordinary class constructors.

java-fundamentals-sr7-03.reason: tell: removes the 'fits a parameter declared as' template, which carries two false cards (sr7-03, sr8-01) and the permission-verb tell. Same fact (generic invariance) and answer (false). (final: keep)
java-fundamentals-sr7-03.statement: A `List<Integer>` value is assignable to a variable of type `List<Number>`.
java-fundamentals-sr7-03.explanation: Java rejects assigning a List<Integer> to a List<Number> variable. A subtype relationship between element classes does not transfer to these parameterized types.
java-fundamentals-sr7-03.misconception: Generic containers inherit the subtype relationships of their element types.
